label: Three stories to carry in your pocket

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Facts are great, but I want stories.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Give me three I can tell somebody over a coffee.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Okay. Story one. A night raid.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Ooh.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1356, the Count of Flanders invades Brussels and takes it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A citizen called Everard t'Serclaes, from one of the great families, leads a night raid with a small band of men, slips into the city, and drives the Flemish garrison out.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A local hero.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A very local one. There's a monument to him in the Rue Charles Buls, just off the Grand Place.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the tradition is that you touch the bronze for luck.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll be touching it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Everyone does. It's shiny. Story two.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A night at the opera.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Two nights, two stories.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: On the twenty-fifth of August, 1830, there's a performance at the Théâtre de la Monnaie of a popular French opera called The Mute Girl of Portici.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's about a revolt against Spanish rule in seventeenth-century Naples, and it has a stirring duet about love of country.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the audience took it personally.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They poured out into the street, and the unrest turned into a revolution.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Within weeks, the southern provinces of the Netherlands had broken away, and Belgium was an independent country with Brussels as its capital.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: From a duet to a country.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Story three is smaller. It's Saint Gudula, the patron saint of the city.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The legend says she walked to church before dawn carrying a lantern, and the devil kept blowing it out, and each time an angel lit it again.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And that's the patron saint of a whole capital.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A woman, a lantern, and a stubborn angel.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It tells you something about the city's character.
